subject: Accountancy
central_question: How are the legal relationship of partners, their capital accounts and the appropriation of partnership profit recorded fairly under the partnership deed and the Indian Partnership Act, 1932?
in_scope_units: Nature of partnership, its statutory definition and essential features including mutual agency and unlimited liability.
Partnership deed, its usual clauses and the accounting rules that apply when the deed is silent.
Special aspects of partnership accounts and maintenance of partners’ capital accounts under fixed and fluctuating methods.
Distribution of profit through the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account, including salary, commission and interest adjustments.
Calculation and treatment of interest on capital under additions, withdrawals, insufficient profit and loss.
Calculation of interest on drawings using average-period and product methods for monthly, quarterly and irregular drawings.
Guarantee of a minimum profit to a partner and allocation of the resulting deficiency.
Past adjustments through a Profit and Loss Adjustment Account or direct capital-account adjustment.
banned_topics: Admission, retirement and death of partners, which are covered in later reconstitution chapters.
Realisation of assets and settlement on dissolution, which belongs to Dissolution of Partnership Firm.
Issue of shares or debentures by companies, which belongs to company accounts.

known_pitfalls.claim: Partners must contribute equal capital and therefore always share profits equally.
known_pitfalls.correction: Capital contribution and profit sharing are separate matters. The deed governs the ratio; only when it is silent are profits and losses shared equally.

known_pitfalls.claim: A partner is automatically entitled to salary and interest on capital.
known_pitfalls.correction: Salary, commission and interest on capital are allowed only when authorised by the partnership deed and are subject to the chapter’s treatment of available profit.

known_pitfalls.claim: Under the fixed capital method all partner-related items are posted to the capital account.
known_pitfalls.correction: Only permanent capital additions and withdrawals affect the fixed capital account; drawings, interest, salary, commission and profit share are posted to the current account.

known_pitfalls.claim: If the deed is silent, no interest is allowed on a partner’s loan.
known_pitfalls.correction: The Act allows interest on a partner’s loan at 6 per cent per annum when the deed is silent.

recommended_example_progression: Use Test Your Understanding–I to apply the Act when the deed is silent.
Use NCERT Illustration 1 to compare fixed and fluctuating capital accounts.
Use NCERT Illustration 2 to prepare the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account.
Use NCERT Illustration 7 to examine interest on capital when profit is absent or insufficient.
Use NCERT Illustration 8 for monthly and irregular drawings and NCERT Illustration 10 for a profit guarantee.
Use NCERT Illustration 14 to pass a single past-adjustment entry.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Questions for Practice containing Short Answer Questions 1–7, Long Answer Questions 1–5 and Numerical Questions on capital accounts, appropriation, interest, guarantees and past adjustments.
